 MP calls for reports on flood mitigation projects in Klang Valley
 18-Nov-2026, 13:56 18 Nov 2026, 13:56 Dineskumar Ragu Share Klang MP V Ganabatirau says the success of flood mitigation projects should be measured by how many areas are no longer flooded.
 Heavy rain triggered flash floods in 23 areas across four districts in Selangor yesterday. (Bernama pic) 
 KUALA LUMPUR : Klang MP V Ganabatirau has urged the energy transition and water transformation ministry (Petra) to table reports on the progress and effectiveness of flood mitigation projects, particularly in his constituency and the Klang Valley. 
 Debating Petra’s 2027 budget at the committee stage in the Dewan Rakyat today, Ganabatirau said four flood mitigation projects currently underway in Klang were scheduled for completion in 2029, but their progress rates ranged from just 1.21% to 12.09%.
 The Pakatan Harapan lawmaker asked whether Petra assessed contractors’ performance based on the actual effectiveness of their projects or merely the projects’ progress and contract payments.
 He asked whether the ministry conducted audits after the projects are completed to measure reductions in flood frequency, water levels, the extent of affected areas and losses suffered by residents.
 “The success of flood mitigation projects should not be measured by how many billions of ringgit have been announced, but by how many areas are no longer flooded.
 “The people of Klang have waited too long. They no longer want to just hear announcements. They want to see solutions.”
 Heavy rain triggered flash floods in 23 areas across four districts in Selangor yesterday.
 Eight of the affected districts were in Klang, followed by Gombak (seven), Kuala Selangor (five) and Petaling (three).
 Among the affected routes were the Federal Highway near i-City in Shah Alam and Bulatan Klang, where rising water levels made driving difficult for motorists.
